forms: pick the trait from a short story
tell a trait from a feeling
say how a value shapes a trait
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.SOCIAL.SELF_IMPROVEMENT.PERSONAL.mastery: The child names traits (honest, confident, shy, patient, optimistic, hardworking, impatient) from what a person does, tells a trait (how a person usually is) from a feeling (how a person is at one moment), and says values such as honesty and respect shape traits. The child does not say traits can never change. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what self-esteem is
pick a sign of healthy self-esteem
pick an effect of low or inflated self-esteem
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.SOCIAL.SELF_ESTEEM_ASSESSMENT.SE.mastery: The child says self-esteem is how a person values themselves, picks signs of healthy self-esteem (trying new things, accepting mistakes, respecting others) and of unhealthy self-esteem (low: withdrawing, giving up, being bullied; inflated: boasting, looking down on others), and does not say self-esteem means boasting. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.COMMUN.COMMUNITY_SERVICE_LEARNI..mastery: The child puts the steps in order (identify a problem or gap, design a solution, plan how to carry it out, carry out the plan, report on the project), says what each step does, and does not skip planning or write the report before the work. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the early humans in order
say what changed
say what the evidence is
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.PEOPLE.SCIENTIFIC_THEORY_ABOUT_..mastery: The child says the scientific theory is that humans slowly changed (evolved) over millions of years from earlier ape-like ancestors, puts the early humans in order (Australopithecus, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo sapiens), names the changes (walking upright, a bigger brain, making and using tools, using fire) and the evidence (fossils and tools). The child does not say humans come from the monkeys alive today. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a reason for Africa
pick a famous site
pick how remains are preserved
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.PEOPLE.SCIENTIFIC_THEORY_ABOUT_..mastery: The child says the oldest fossils of early humans have been found in Africa, in East Africa's Rift Valley (Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania, Koobi Fora near Lake Turkana in Kenya) and elsewhere in Africa, names the Leakey family and the Turkana Boy, and picks ways to preserve remains (protected sites, careful digging, museums, labels and records, controlled storage). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a Swahili city-state
say what the Swahili traded and with whom
say what the civilisation gave us
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.PEOPLE.EARLY_CIVILISATION.SWAHIL.mastery: The child names Swahili city-states (Mombasa, Malindi, Lamu, Kilwa, Zanzibar), says the Swahili traded gold, ivory, cloth, timber and other goods by dhow with Arabia, Persia, India and China using the monsoon winds, built coral-stone houses and mosques, and gave the Kiswahili language and a coastal culture. The child does not say Kiswahili is Arabic. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a factor
say how it was carried out
pick an effect
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.PEOPLE.TRANS_SAHARAN_SLAVE_TRAD..mastery: The child says the trade crossed the Sahara by camel caravans between West and Central Africa and North Africa, names factors (a demand for labour in North Africa and beyond, raiding and wars, the camel and the desert trade routes), says caravans were led by guides and traders along routes with oases, and names effects (loss of lives, families broken, villages emptied, fear and insecurity). The child does not say the trade went by sea. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a cause of growth
pick an effect of growth
pick a type of migration
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G8.PEOPLE.POPULATION_GROWTH_IN_AFR..mastery: The child says population grows when births are more than deaths (a high birth rate, fewer deaths from better health care and food) and by people moving in, names effects (pressure on land, food, houses, schools and jobs), tells types of migration (rural-urban, between countries, forced by war or drought and by choice), and says Kenya had about 47.6 million people at the 2019 census and a young population. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
